integrations.osc: TRANSPORT AND APPLICATION BOTH EXIST, THEY ARE NOT CONNECTED. UDP receive is real (osc.rs, 127.0.0.1:9000) and OSC->engine application is real (GuiCommand::LiveOsc -> control::apply_to_dispatcher, app/src/commands.rs:478). What is missing is the wire between them: nothing converts a received OscControl into a LiveOsc dispatch, integrations::apply_controls and app::control::apply_osc have no non-test callers, and the desktop process never opens a receiver at all. `flux osc <port>` only prints. There is also no OSC output path (encode_param_feedback is test-only; port 9001 unused). Note LiveOsc is a no-op unless a LearnBinding set control_map.graph_id first.

ci_defects_found_2026_11_14: HEAD DOES NOT PASS ITS OWN CI. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is the first check step in ci.yml (line 29, 'Format check') and the first step of verify.ps1 (line 32); at e84fe67 it exits 1 with 56 diffs across 12 files (src-tauri build.rs + lib.rs, app/commands.rs, app/samples.rs, catalog/presets.rs, media/lib.rs, and tests export_formats/golden/node_editor/preset_sweep/preview_perf/sweep_catalog). The compact hand-formatted multi-item arrays and long assert! lines committed on 2026-11-10 (fe9e35e, ac73572, 8139007) were never rustfmt-ed. In GitHub Actions a failing step aborts the job, so every step after 'Format check' - including the whole workspace test suite - would not run.

verify.ps1:35 masks two of its three exit codes. The 'integration-tests' Step block runs three cargo tests separated by `;`, and Step only reads $LASTEXITCODE after the block - so the step's ok reflects dag_parallel (the last command) alone. Measured directly: a block containing a failing `cargo fmt` then a passing `doctor` records ok=True exit=0. A producer_tests or export_matrix regression is invisible in verify.json.

verify.json records skipped gates as ok:true. link-integration and spout-enumeration write { ok = true; skipped = true } when their env vars are unset, which is exactly the AGENTS.md rule 'missing prerequisite is blocked_external, never passed' violated inside the verification harness itself. The aggregate ok can never reflect an unavailable SDK.

The step name 'ndi-discovery' overpromises. It runs `cargo test -p flux-integrations --features ndi ndi::`, which selects exactly 2 tests (runtime_loads_and_initializes, discovery_returns_state_without_crash). crates/integrations/src/ndi.rs contains no other test. So the repeatable NDI evidence is 'the DLL loads and discovery does not crash' - the 'discovery of 5 live sources + live send/receive cross-process' claim came from an ad-hoc manual run that no test reproduces.

clippy is neutered: ci.yml:31 runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -A warnings` (-A = allow), so it can only detect a compile failure, never a lint. The plain build already emits ~10 warnings, including dead fields in RuntimeGraph and a never-used flux_app_persistence_load.

xtask benchmark lies about what it measured (crates/xtask/src/main.rs:299-382). (a) `--profile` is parsed and echoed into the JSON but never used - resolution is hardcoded 1920x1080 at :331/:355 and the sample set is `.take(30)` fragment generators at :324, so `--profile ordinary` and a hypothetical `--profile 4k` do identical work. (b) Each timed iteration includes a full 1920x1080 readback (:371), so p50/p95 are render + an ~8 MB GPU->CPU copy, not render cost, and are not comparable to a frame budget. (c) With 12 samples, `times[len*95/100]` = index 11 = the single worst sample, so 'p95' is really max and 'p50' is index 6. The headline 'gen.concentric p95 21.49 ms' is one outlier of twelve.
